record.original_question: How to decide whether eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed in the result that was mentioned above?

evidence.quote: How to decide whether eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed in the result that was mentioned above?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ be a primitive morphism, i.e. a monoid homomorphism whose incidence (composition) matrix $M_h\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{\Sigma\times\Sigma}$, defined by $(M_h)_{a,b}=|h(b)|_a$ (the number of occurrences of letter $a$ in $h(b)$), is primitive (some power has all entries strictly positive). Suppose $a\in\Sigma$ satisfies $h(a)=au$ for some non-empty $u$, so that $h$ admits the infinite fixed point $h^\infty(a)=\lim_{n\to\infty}h^n(a)\in\Sigma^\omega$.

A template $t$ over $\Sigma$ is, in the standard sense of abelian pattern realization, a finite combinatorial object specifying constraints on the Parikh vectors of factors of an infinite word; one says that $h^\infty(a)$ realizes $t$ if there exists a factorization of some factor of $h^\infty(a)$ whose Parikh vectors satisfy the linear/affine constraints encoded by $t$ (this captures abelian repetitions, abelian-$k$-powers, additive powers, and similar abelian patterns).

It is known that whenever every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $M_h$ satisfies $|\lambda|\neq 1$, there is an algorithm that, given $h$ and any template $t$, decides whether $h^\infty(a)$ realizes $t$.

Question: Is there an algorithm which, on input a primitive morphism $h$ (with a fixed point $h^\infty(a)$) whose matrix $M_h$ is allowed to have eigenvalues of complex norm $1$, together with a template $t$, decides whether $h^\infty(a)$ realizes $t$? Equivalently, can the hypothesis "$M_h$ has no eigenvalue of norm $1$" be removed from the above decidability result?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an explicitly listed open problem in the WORDS-conference open-problems compilation (arXiv:1705.04055 / hal-02355621). The underlying decidability result of Rao and Rosenfeld (2015) requires the no-eigenvalue-of-norm-1 hypothesis, and recent surveys on abelian combinatorics on words still list the eigenvalue-of-norm-1 case as unresolved. No source verifying a resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Rao and Rosenfeld proved that for any primitive morphism h whose matrix has no eigenvalue of norm 1 and any template t, it is possible to decide if h^infty(a) realizes t. How to decide if eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed?
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem following the Rao–Rosenfeld decidability result.

status_evidence.title: Abelian combinatorics on words: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian combinatorics on words discussing decidability of pattern realization for morphic words.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey treats the topic without indicating a resolution of the eigenvalue-of-norm-1 case.
